title: console.py concentrates the widest fan-in and the highest rework rate in the package
symptom: 2699 LOC, 116 functions, max nesting 11, fan-in 110 — the 100th percentile of this repository. 463 edits, more than any other file, and a Wilson lower bound on the rework rate of 0.50: half of the changes to this file come back as a fix within days, against a repository-wide 0.263.
cost_pain: rework_rate_lb 0.50 against 0.263 for the repository, on its most-edited file (463 edits, median fix latency 4.13 days)
cost_spread: fan_in 110 of 213 files — every second file in the package imports it
remedy: Extract the render pipeline (segment assembly and the render_* helpers) into its own module and leave Console a facade that delegates. An extraction with the public API unchanged, not a redesign.
remedy_cost: High. 110 importers, and `from rich.console import Console` is the documented public surface — the split has to be invisible from outside.
gain: Half of the change traffic to console.py stops returning as a fix within the week.
refutation: L1 argues a facade earns its fan-in; kept because the pain is measured on the behaviour axis rather than inferred from the fan-in. L4 is the real constraint and is recorded in remedy_cost.

title: one function in pretty.py carries cyclomatic complexity 76
symptom: cyclomatic_per_function_max 76 with nesting 9 in a 1017-line file; the worst function starts at line 580. Fix share 0.19 over 156 edits puts the file in the 84th percentile of this repository for the share of edits that are fixes.
cost_pain: fix_share 0.19 (84th percentile) across 156 edits — the file is not merely long, its edits are disproportionately corrective
cost_spread: Local. pretty.py is not in the hub list; the complexity is paid inside the file.
remedy: Replace the branch cascade in the function at line 580 with a dispatch table keyed by the node type it is switching on.
remedy_cost: Moderate and contained in one file; the function has no callers outside the module.
gain: The worst function drops below the McCabe threshold the catalogue uses for a per-function flag.
refutation: L2 checked: the threshold is per function, not per file, so the 1017 LOC do not carry the finding — 76 is one function.

title: a 50-file strongly connected component survives removing the package barrel
symptom: structure.cycles reports one runtime SCC of 53 files. Recomputing it with rich/__init__.py removed still leaves 50: the cycle is not an artefact of `from rich import ...` edges through the barrel, which is the usual explanation for a large SCC in a Python package.
cost_pain: Not established. The files inside the SCC are also the most edited files in the repository, so this measurement cannot separate the cost of the cycle from the cost of console.py being large.
cost_spread: 50 of 213 files cannot be isolated from one another
remedy: None proposed. A remedy for an unpriced problem is a guess, and the catalogue forbids issuing one.
gain: Unmeasured. Recorded so the next run can tell whether the SCC shrinks on its own.
refutation: L3 demoted it to a hypothesis: the pain that co-occurs with the SCC is fully explained by F1, and the measurement cannot attribute any of it to the cycle itself.
